{{Current events|year=2021|month=02|day=13|content=
<!-- All news items below this line -->
'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–present)|War in Afghanistan]]
**[[2021 Afghanistan attacks]]
***At least four security forces personnel, including a commander, are killed in eastern and southern [[Afghanistan]] as clashes with an unidentified [[terrorist group]] intensify. Separately, in [[Kandahar Province|Kandahar]], a [[Humvee]] containing explosives detonates, injuring seven [[Afghan National Police|police]] officers. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-afghanistan-attack/clashes-blasts-intensify-across-afghanistan-idUSKBN2AD06D?il=0 (Reuters)]

'''Arts and culture'''
*[[Egypt]]ian and American [[archaeologist]]s discover an ancient [[mass-production]] [[brewery]] in the [[ancient Egypt]]ian city of [[Abydos, Egypt|Abydos]], likely dating back to the [[Early Dynastic Period (Egypt)|Early Dynastic Period]]. [[Mostafa Waziri]], the secretary-general of the Egyptian [[Supreme Council of Antiquities]], believes it to be "the oldest high-production brewery in the world". [https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1395568/egypt-unearths-worlds-oldest-mass-production-brewery (AFP via ''Philippine Daily Inquirer'')]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*[[2021 Fukushima earthquake]]
**A 7.3 magnitude [[list of earthquakes in Japan|earthquake]] strikes off the [[Tōhoku]] coast of [[Japan]], injuring at least 110 people. [https://www.japantimes.co.jp/news/2021/02/13/national/earthquake-fukushima/ (''The Japan Times'')]
*A series of severe weather-related incidents in [[Northern Italy]] leaves four people dead and 25 others injured. [https://www.ilmessaggero.it/italia/meteo_diretta_burian_oggi_previsioni_neve_lazio_maltempo_vento_news-5764255.html (''Il Messaggero'')]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Lebanon]]
****[[Lebanon]] receives their first shipment of 28,500 doses of the [[Pfizer-BioNTech COVID-19 vaccine|Pfizer-BioNTech]] [[COVID-19 vaccine|vaccine]] from [[Belgium]]. [https://www.arabnews.com/node/1808656/middle-east (''Arab News'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Pakistan]]
****Two 11-week-old [[white tiger]] cubs that died in [[Lahore Zoo]] on January 30 appear to have died of [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/two-white-tiger-cubs-in-pakistan-likely-died-of-covid-19-zoo-officials-101613205938098-amp.html (''Hindustan Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Korea]]
****The [[Government of South Korea|government]] decides to lower [[social distancing]] levels to level 2 in the [[Seoul Capital Area]] and level 1.5 in other regions beginning February 15, allowing nightclubs to reopen and extending the operating hours of restaurants, coffee shops and gyms in the Seoul Capital Area until 10 pm local time. However, gatherings of more than five people continue to be prohibited but [[theatre]]s, [[Library|libraries]], and other types of businesses will no longer be subject to operating hours restrictions. [https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2021-02-13/south-korea-to-ease-social-distancing-in-bid-to-help-small-biz (Bloomberg)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in the United Arab Emirates]]
****The [[United Arab Emirates]] surpasses 1,000 deaths from [[COVID-19]]. [https://www.khaleejtimes.com/coronavirus-pandemic/coronavirus-uae-reports-2631-covid-19-cases-3589-recoveries-15-deaths (''Khaleej Times'')]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Canada]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Prince Edward Island]]
****[[Prince Edward Island]] reports their first case of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] in a man in his 20s who had travelled internationally. [https://www.cbc.ca/news/canada/prince-edward-island/pei-covid19-briefing-feb-13-1.5913595 (CBC)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Australia]]
***[[Victoria (Australia)|Victoria]] returns to Stage 4 restrictions in a five-day "circuit breaker" [[COVID-19 lockdowns|lockdown]] due to an ongoing outbreak of the [[Variant of Concern 202012/01|B.1.1.7 variant]] at the [[Melbourne Airport]] [[Holiday Inn]]. All non-essential businesses are closed, masks are mandatory in all public places, and people are only permitted to leave their homes for essential work, education or care-giving, or for up to 2 hours a day for essential shopping and outdoor exercise within a 5 km (3.1 mi) radius of their homes. All [[international flight]]s to [[Melbourne]] have also been cancelled for the duration of the lockdown. [https://www.abc.net.au/news/2021-02-12/victoria-coronavirus-lockdown-announced-by-daniel-andrews/13128514 (ABC Australia)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Northern Cyprus]]
***[[Northern Cyprus]] extends their full-scale curfew until February 22 in order to reduce the spread of COVID-19. [https://www.aa.com.tr/en/latest-on-coronavirus-outbreak/northern-cyprus-extends-curfew-to-feb-22/2144085# (Anadolu Agency)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in South Africa]]
***The [[Second Cabinet of Cyril Ramaphosa|cabinet]] announces that 20 of [[South Africa]]'s land borders with [[Botswana]], [[Lesotho]], [[Eswatini]], [[Namibia]], [[Mozambique]] and [[Zimbabwe]] will reopen on February 15. [https://www.timeslive.co.za/news/south-africa/2021-02-13-20-land-borders-will-reopen-on-monday-says-motsoaledi/ (TimesLIVE)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Venezuela]]
***[[Venezuela]] receives their first shipment of 100,000 doses of the [[Sputnik V COVID-19 vaccine|Sputnik V]] [[COVID-19|vaccine]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/instant-article/idUSKBN2AD0MY (Reuters)]
*[[Guinea]]'s [[Ministry of Health (Guinea)|health ministry]] reports the country's first deaths from the [[Ebola]] virus disease since the [[Western African Ebola virus epidemic|2013–2016 epidemic]]. [https://www.hindustantimes.com/world-news/guinea-suffers-first-ebola-deaths-since-2016-101613253595474.html (AFP via ''Hindustan Times'')]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Second impeachment trial of Donald Trump]]
**The [[United States Senate]] votes to acquit former [[President of the United States|president]] [[Donald Trump]] for the second time when the 57–43 vote in favor of conviction fails to reach the necessary two-thirds majority. Seven Republicans join the entire Democratic caucus in voting for conviction, making it the closest trial vote since the [[Impeachment of Andrew Johnson|Andrew Johnson impeachment trial]] of 1868. [https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/538750-senate-gop-acquits-trump-for-second-time (The Hill)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[2021 Italian government crisis]], [[Draghi Cabinet]]
**[[Prime Minister of Italy|Prime Minister]] [[Mario Draghi]] and the ministers of his cabinet are officially sworn in at the [[Quirinal Palace]] in [[Rome]], ending the [[2021 Italian government crisis|government crisis]]. [https://www.ansa.it/sito/notizie/politica/2021/02/13/governo-draghi-giuramento-ministri-mattarella-quirinale-campanella-cdm_1a9d65c0-fb3e-4950-949b-4ebf0a587710.html (ANSA)]
*[[Presidency of Joe Biden]]
**[[White House Deputy Press Secretary]] [[TJ Ducklo]] resigns after making threats towards ''[[Politico]]'' journalist [[Tara Palmeri]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-56058477 (BBC)]

'''Sports'''
*[[2021 Australian Open]], [[Impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on sports]]
**Spectators at a late-running tennis match are ordered to leave as Victoria's 5-day "circuit breaker" lockdown comes into effect. Matches at the [[Melbourne]] tournament will continue without any spectators for the duration of the lockdown. [https://wwos.nine.com.au/tennis/melbourne-covid-restrictions-australian-open-crowd-sent-home/5d07160c-2e18-491d-892a-71ad6a2f451a (9 News)]
